title: iPad
alt: Maybe we're all gonna die, but we're gonna die in *really cool ways*.
transcript:
[Cueball is sitting in an armchair, playing with an iPad. Megan is looking over his shoulder.]
Cueball: Navigating Google Maps on the iPad is fun. It feels so futuristic.
Cueball: Swoosh! Zoom!

[Close-up on Megan.]
Megan: There are, right now, monkeys controlling robotic arms via neural implants.

Megan: A huge and alien future is barreling toward us. And I can't wait.

[Zoom-out on both characters. Cueball is still looking down on his iPad.]
Megan: But no, your iPad is cool, too.
Cueball: Stop spoiling my future with your slightly more distant one.
explanation:
In this comic, Cueball is entertained by his  (which came out a few days prior to this comic) by messing around with  because he thinks "zooming around" the globe via panning around the map feels futuristic. Megan tries to bring perspective to him by telling him that there are so many more futuristic things in the (possible) near future. Cueball still objects, because that makes him feel that he's too easily impressed by trivial things, and says that Megan is spoiling his fun by trying to make his source of entertainment seem so mundane compared to "monkeys controlling robotic arms via neural implants".

The title text shows how either Cueball or Megan are, like a scientist, enthralled by the many "really cool" ways that death could occur, instead of being horrified by any new ways to die such advances in technology could present.
